We need number of C=O groups. IR spectrum shows peaks; carbonyl typically around 1700 cm-1 (C=O stretch). The given wavenumbers: 3407 (OH/NH), 3045-2927 (C-H), 2356, 2221, 1511, 1507. No peak near 1700. There is 2356 (maybe CO2), 2221 (C≡N or alkyne). No carbonyl. So answer 0.

But ensure no hidden carbonyl maybe in other region not listed. The IR data limited. Could also use carbon NMR to see carbonyl carbon ~190-210 ppm. Could check carbon NMR to confirm. But IR already suggests none. To be safe, maybe get carbon NMR to see if any carbonyl signals. Use carbon_nmr_spectra tool (expensive but cheap). Let's do it to confirm.
